description: We are a Chilean team passionate about space exploration, Earth science, data and technology. We want to use NASA and planetary data to explore how extreme Earth environments can support future Moon and Mars missions. We’re looking for teammates with skills in Earth Science, GIS, data analysis, coding, AI/ML, web development, visualization, design and storytelling.
summary: AnalogOS helps planetary robotics teams answer a practical question: which Earth sector deserves reconnaissance for a specific Mars rover test, and why? Our working prototype turns a test brief into user-confirmed requirements, evaluates them against traceable observations, and shows what meets the conditions, what fails, and what remains unmeasured. A reproducible Chile-Argentina pilot screened 50 terrain windows, shortlisted six candidates, and retained Pampa Yungay as a known reference rather than a new discovery. NASA MOLA supplies the Jezero reference; NASADEM, NASA POWER and Copernicus Sentinel-2 characterize Earth terrain and context. Official SERNAGEOMIN and SEGEMAR geology supports cited field-check recommendations selected by optional AI. Scores and eligibility decisions remain deterministic. Interactive maps, explicit limitations and downloadable evidence make the reasoning inspectable. AnalogOS addresses the challenge through a bounded Mars-analog workflow that can be extended to other regions and mission profiles. It supports early campaign planning, not site certification, access permission or a claim that Earth reproduces every Martian condition.
details:
ANALOGOS — FROM A TEST OBJECTIVE TO A DEFENSIBLE FIELD SHORTLIST

THE PROBLEM AND OUR USER

Planetary robotics researchers, university rover teams and campaign planners need to choose where to test navigation, perception and mobility before committing to a field campaign. A famous Mars-like landscape is not enough: a site must support the particular experiment, and the team must know which observations support the choice and which checks remain open. AnalogOS connects the question, the evidence and the next field investigation.

HOW IT ADDRESSES THE CHALLENGE

We implement a focused part of identifying terrestrial analog locations: early screening for Mars rover tests using a regional Jezero reference. The current execution is a Chile-Argentina pilot, not a completed global search. We do not claim to have selected a permanent Moon or Mars base. Lunar profiles, additional countries and other experiments are future extensions requiring their own evidence and validation.

TWO WAYS TO START

1. Describe a test. Optional AI assistance proposes editable requirements anchored to the user's words. The user confirms the actual thresholds and importance before evaluation; the free-text brief is not silently treated as a measured specification.

2. Select a sector. Explore the available windows or request a point/rectangle. The system makes the requested geometry and the geometry supported by data explicit. It does not acquire new measurements or attribute an entire window's geology to a small point or arbitrary polygon.

The result distinguishes prioritized, excluded and insufficient-evidence cases, explains every requirement, and retains unmeasured needs such as traction and permits as pending.

NASA DATA AND THE REPRODUCIBLE SEARCH

NASA PDS Mars Global Surveyor MOLA MEGDR provides regional elevation around Jezero. NASADEM supplies Earth elevation; it is aggregated to a comparable scale of roughly 460-480 metres before comparing regional slope, roughness and local relief. A documented grid search evaluated 50 windows of roughly 20 km across interior Antofagasta and the Puna of Catamarca and Salta, covering approximately 22,274 square kilometres. Four windows containing published sampling coordinates left the candidate ranking; the final shortlist has three candidates per country. Pampa Yungay remains a known reference, outside the discovery ranking. No candidate is claimed to be a newly discovered analog.

Twelve monthly Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A mosaics from 2025 describe non-vegetated surface and seasonal context. NASA POWER supplies regional precipitation and surface-temperature climatology for 2001-2025. NASA HLS/CMR provides an independent availability inventory; HLS and Blue Marble imagery also provide visual context through NASA GIBS. Image display is separate from scientific scoring.

GEOLOGY AND THE ROLE OF AI

Official SERNAGEOMIN geology distributed by Chile's MMA and SEGEMAR/SIGAM geology for Argentina add original mapped units, descriptions, source links, map scale, coverage gaps and overlaps. An optional AI call receives the confirmed objective and this official context. It selects references from a closed catalogue of field checks: for example, checking map-to-ground correspondence or measuring surface material where a named unit is mapped. Each recommendation retains its source and limitations. The model cannot invent measurements, change the deterministic assessment or restore an excluded sector. Invalid selections are rejected.

A verified example in the Argentine pilot selected checks involving the Galan volcanic complex and alluvial/colluvial deposits while keeping traction unmeasured. Contrasting mobility and lithological-sampling objectives produced different, valid selections. These demonstrations test software behaviour; they do not establish field suitability.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

AnalogOS searches instead of merely listing well-known analog sites, compares Earth and Mars at compatible spatial scales, preserves known precedents, and ties recommendations to a specific test. Similarity, evidence confidence and territorial feasibility remain separate. Missing data is visible. Each result can be exported as an auditable report containing the request, evaluation, evidence, source identities and optional AI provenance. The manual workflow, local maps and packaged datasets work offline; AI requires a connection and a configured server.

IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION

The prototype uses Python geospatial pipelines with NumPy, pyproj, Shapely, earthaccess and JSON Schema; React, TypeScript and Vite for the interface; three.js/React Three Fiber and MapLibre for visual exploration, with local fallback maps; and a server-side Anthropic integration. Public data are processed into versioned snapshots with provenance and integrity checks. The reviewed implementation passed 316 Python and 332 web tests, type checks and a production build. We also checked real AI responses, downloaded-report reconstruction, offline operation and mobile presentation.

IMPACT AND LIMITS

Our intended benefit is to make early site selection more transparent and reduce avoidable scouting effort; no field cost or time saving has yet been measured. Regional topography cannot reveal wheel-scale obstacles. Sentinel-2 surface classes and mapped rock units do not measure soil mechanics. NASA POWER's climate cell is larger than a candidate window. Gravity, atmospheric pressure, radiation and exact Martian chemistry are not reproduced. Geological field validation, ownership, protected areas, safe access and permits remain necessary.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE DISCLOSURE

OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude assisted research, software implementation, debugging, tests, interface design, documentation, translation and presentation preparation. AI-assisted code processes observations from cited providers; we do not present synthetic values as satellite measurements. The running product uses Anthropic for proposed requirements and selection of existing evidence and geological checks. The team reviews the work and users confirm requirements; scientific scores and evaluations are calculated by explicit code, not generated by a language model. AI-assisted output is identified in the interface and exported provenance.

LINKS AND REPRODUCTION

The Project link points to the latest reviewed code and data on the dev branch, including the portable offline ZIP, evidence exports, source manifests and method decisions. Public application: https://analogos.vercel.app/ . Project overview: https://analogos-landing.vercel.app/ . The demonstration link opens the existing 29.95-second video directly. The public application may lag the reviewed branch; the repository is the authoritative version for the capabilities described here. No NASA endorsement or field certification is claimed.
